chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Make this matter of yours for the sake of Allah, and do not make it for the people, for whatever is for Allah is for Allah, and whatever is for the people, it does not ascend to the sky.'
And do not dispute with the people regarding your Religion, for disputing is a sickness of the heart.
Surely you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah Guides whom He Desires.
Will you then force the people until they become Believers?

Leave off the people, for the people are taking (their Religion) from the people, and you all are taking from Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and Ali (peace be upon him), and there is no equation.
And indeed I heard my father saying: 'When Allah Ordains for a servant to enter into this matter (Al-Wilayah), he would be quicker to it than the bird to its nest'.

key_terms.لِلنَّاسِ: For the people / For public display
key_terms.لِلَّهِ: For the sake of Allah / Dedicated to Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of dedicating religious matters to Allah alone and avoiding disputes with people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises believers to dedicate their religious affairs solely to Allah rather than for public display, warning that disputes over religion corrupt the heart. He cites Quranic verses to illustrate that guidance is Allah's domain, not forced by humans, and emphasizes that the Ahl al-Bayt's authority is distinct from the people's derived knowledge. This narration underscores the Shia principle of *al-Tabligh* (conveyance) without compulsion (*Ikrah*), highlighting that the Imams' role is to transmit the divine message faithfully, leaving the actual acceptance of faith to Allah's will.
